subject: chem
title: Biomolecules
syllabus: Carbohydrates: classification (aldoses and ketoses), monosaccharides (glucose and fructose) and constituent monosaccharides of oligosaccharides (sucrose, lactose and maltose). Proteins: elementary idea of α-amino acids, peptide bond, polypeptides; primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary structure (qualitative idea only), denaturation of proteins. Vitamins: classification and functions. Nucleic acids: chemical constitution of DNA and RNA; biological functions of nucleic acids. Hormones: general introduction.

topics.carb: Carbohydrates: glucose, fructose, di- and polysaccharides

body: Glucose C_{6}H_{12}O_{6} is an aldohexose. Evidence for its open chain: HI/heat → n-hexane (straight chain); NH_{2}OH → oxime and HCN → cyanohydrin (C=O); Br_{2} water → gluconic acid (–CHO); Ac_{2}O → pentaacetate (five –OH); HNO_{3} → saccharic acid (–CH_{2}OH at the other end).
But glucose gives no Schiff's test and no NaHSO_{3} adduct, and its pentaacetate does not react with NH_{2}OH: it is mostly a six-membered ring (pyranose) hemiacetal.
α and β glucose differ only at C1 — they are ANOMERS (α +112°, β +19°; in water both slowly reach +52.5°: mutarotation). D/L describes the –OH at the lowest stereocentre, NOT the sign of rotation.
Sucrose = α-glucose C1 – β-fructose C2: both anomeric carbons used → NON-reducing. Hydrolysis gives invert sugar (laevorotatory: fructose −92.4° beats glucose +52.5°).
Maltose (α1→4, glucose + glucose) and lactose (β1→4, galactose + glucose; milk sugar) keep a free hemiacetal → reducing.

Starch = amylose (α1→4, unbranched, ~15–20%) + amylopectin (α1→4 with α1→6 branches). Glycogen ("animal starch") is like amylopectin but more branched. Cellulose = β1→4 glucose (cannot be digested by humans).

α-amino acids H_{2}N–CHR–COOH exist as zwitterions. All except glycine are chiral (natural ones are L). Essential (must be eaten): valine, leucine, isoleucine, phenylalanine, tryptophan, threonine, methionine, lysine, arginine, histidine.

Peptide bond = –CO–NH– formed by losing water. Gly-Ala means glycine's C=O is joined to alanine's N–H (N-terminus written first). n different residues used once give n! sequences; n residues have n − 1 peptide bonds.

HNO_{2} turns –NH_{2} into –OH (alanine → lactic acid). Tyrosine has a phenolic –OH (violet with FeCl_{3}); cysteine's –SH forms –S–S– bridges; proline has a five-membered ring; histidine an imidazole ring.

check.q: Number of peptide bonds in a pentapeptide

body: Primary: amino-acid sequence. Secondary: α-helix / β-pleated sheet (backbone H-bonds). Tertiary: overall fold of one chain (fibrous or globular; H-bonds, –S–S–, ionic, van der Waals). Quaternary: several subunits (haemoglobin).
Denaturation (heat, pH change, acids) breaks secondary and tertiary structure; the PRIMARY structure survives. Boiling egg white (albumin) coagulates it.

Enzymes are mostly globular proteins, highly specific, and lower the activation energy (more than H^{+} does). Maltase: maltose → glucose; invertase: sucrose → glucose + fructose; ninhydrin turns violet with proteins.

check.q: α-helix belongs to which structure level?

body: Nucleoside = base + sugar (glycosidic bond). Nucleotide = nucleoside + phosphate. Nucleotides join by 5′–3′ PHOSPHODIESTER links.

DNA: 2-deoxyribose; bases A, G (purines) and C, T (pyrimidines); double helix, A=T (2 H-bonds), G≡C (3 H-bonds); carries genetic information and self-duplicates. RNA: ribose, U replaces T, usually single-stranded; makes proteins (m-, r-, t-RNA).
Chargaff: in double-stranded DNA %A = %T and %G = %C, so %A + %G = 50%. Chirality of DNA/RNA comes from the D-sugar.

check.q: H-bonds in a DNA segment with 3 G–C and 2 A–T pairs

body: Fat-soluble: A, D, E, K — stored in liver and adipose tissue. Water-soluble: B-group and C — must be taken regularly; of these only B_{12} is stored.
Names: A retinol, B_{1} thiamine, B_{2} riboflavin, B_{6} pyridoxine, B_{12} cyanocobalamin, C ascorbic acid, D calciferol, E tocopherol, K phylloquinone, H biotin.
Deficiency: A night blindness; B_{1} beriberi; B_{2} cheilosis; B_{6} convulsions; B_{12} pernicious anaemia; C scurvy; D rickets; E fragile RBCs; K slow clotting.

check.q: Which vitamin is water-soluble yet stored in the body?

traps: Sucrose is NON-reducing (both anomeric carbons are tied up).
Fructose reduces Tollens even though it is a ketose.
D/L is not the sign of rotation.
Gly-Ala ≠ Ala-Gly: N-terminus is written first.
Nucleotides are joined by phosphodiester bonds, not glycosidic bonds.
Tyrosine is NOT essential; arginine and histidine are (NCERT list).

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I : Wet cotton clothes made of cellulose based carbohydrate take comparatively longer time to get dried than wet nylon polymer based clothes. Statement II : Intermolecular hydrogen bonding with water molecules is more in nylon-based clothes than in the case of cotton clothes. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
sol: Cellulose carries three free –OH per glucose unit → many H-bonds to water → cotton holds water and dries slowly. I true.
Nylon has far fewer H-bonding sites (only –CONH–) → it H-bonds LESS with water. II false.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: D-(+)-glucose + D-(+)-fructose → sucrose (−H_{2}O); sucrose → (hydrolysis) D-(+)-glucose + D-(+)-fructose. Statement II: Invert sugar is formed during sucrose hydrolysis. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
sol: Fructose from sucrose is D-(−)-fructose (laevorotatory), not D-(+). Statement I false.
Hydrolysis flips the sign of rotation (+ → −): the product mixture is "invert sugar". II true.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: The incorrect statement about Glucose is :
sol: Glucose dissolves because of its FIVE –OH groups H-bonding with water, not because of –CHO. Statement 1 is wrong.
It exists as α/β pyranose + open chain in water (2), C_{6} aldose (3), and sucrose = glucose + fructose (4).
o: Glucose is soluble in water because of having aldehyde functional group
Glucose remains in multiple isomeric form in its aqueous solution
Glucose is one of the monomer unit in sucrose

pyq.q: The correct statements are : A. Activation energy for enzyme catalysed hydrolysis of sucrose is lower than that of acid catalysed hydrolysis. B. During denaturation, secondary and tertiary structures of a protein are destroyed but primary structure remains intact. C. Nucleotides are joined together by glycosidic linkage between C_{1} and C_{4} carbons of the pentose sugar. D. Quaternary structure of proteins represents overall folding of the polypeptide chain.
sol: A: enzymes lower E_{a} far more than H^{+} does. True. B: denaturation keeps the peptide bonds (primary structure). True.
C: nucleotides are linked by PHOSPHODIESTER bonds (C5′–C3′). False. D: overall folding of one chain = TERTIARY structure. False.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Fructose does not contain an aldehydic group but still reduces Tollen's reagent. Statement II: In the presence of base, fructose undergoes rearrangement to give glucose. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
sol: Fructose is a ketose, yet it reduces Tollens reagent (it is an α-hydroxy ketone).
Reason: in the alkaline Tollens medium it isomerises (via an enediol) to glucose/mannose, which carry –CHO. Both true.
o: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

pyq.q: The carbohydrate "Ribose" present in DNA, is A. A pentose sugar B. present in pyranose form C. in "D" configuration D. a reducing sugar, when free E. in α-anomeric form
sol: The nucleic-acid sugar (ribose / 2-deoxyribose) is a pentose (A), of D-series (C), and free it has a hemiacetal → reducing (D).
In nucleotides it is a FURANOSE ring (B false) and the base is attached β (E false).

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I : D-glucose pentaacetate reacts with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine. Statement II : Starch, on heating with concentrated sulfuric acid at 100 °C and 2-3 atmosphere pressure produces glucose. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
sol: Glucose pentaacetate has no free –OH at C1, so the ring cannot open to –CHO: no 2,4-DNP, no NH_{2}OH reaction. I false.
Industrial glucose: starch + dil. H_{2}SO_{4} at 393 K under 2–3 atm. II true (as worded).
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

pyq.q: Match List - I (Saccharides) with List - II (Glycosidic linkages found): (A) Sucrose (B) Maltose (C) Lactose (D) Amylopectin; (I) α1−4 (II) α1−4 and α1−6 (III) α1−β2 (IV) β1−4
sol: Sucrose: C1 of α-glucose to C2 of β-fructose. Maltose: α1→4 (two glucose). Lactose: β1→4 (galactose–glucose).
Amylopectin: α1→4 chains with α1→6 branches.

pyq.q: Identify correct conversion during acidic hydrolysis from the following : (A) starch gives galactose. (B) cane sugar gives equal amount of glucose and fructose. (C) milk sugar gives glucose and galactose. (D) amylopectin gives glucose and fructose. (E) amylose gives only glucose.
sol: Starch (amylose + amylopectin) is all glucose: A and D false, E true.
Cane sugar = sucrose → glucose + fructose 1 : 1 (B). Milk sugar = lactose → glucose + galactose (C).

pyq.q: Match List - I (Carbohydrate) with List - II (Linkage, Source): (A) Amylose (B) Cellulose (C) Glycogen (D) Amylopectin; (I) β−C1−C4, plant (II) α−C1−C4, animal (III) α−C1−C4, α−C1−C6, plant (IV) α−C1−C4, plant
sol: Amylose: unbranched α1→4, plant. Cellulose: β1→4, plant.
Glycogen is "animal starch" — listed here as α1→4, animal. Amylopectin: α1→4 + α1→6 branches, plant.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Sucrose is dextrorotatory. However, sucrose upon hydrolysis gives a solution having mixture of products. This solution shows laevorotation. Statement II: Hydrolysis of sucrose gives glucose and fructose. Since the laevorotation of glucose is more than the dextrorotation of fructose, the resulting solution becomes laevorotatory. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
sol: Sucrose +66.5°; after hydrolysis the mixture is laevorotatory (invert sugar). I true.
II has it backwards: glucose is DEXTRO (+52.5°) and fructose is LAEVO (−92.4°); fructose wins. II false.
o: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

pyq.q: Sugar which does not give reddish brown precipitate with Fehling's reagent is:
sol: Fehling test needs a free (or ring-opening) carbonyl.
In sucrose both anomeric carbons (C1 of glucose, C2 of fructose) are tied in the glycosidic bond → non-reducing.

pyq.q: Match List I with List II: A. Glucose/NaHCO_{3}/Δ B. Glucose/HNO_{3} C. Glucose/HI/Δ D. Glucose/Bromine water; I. Gluconic acid II. No reaction III. n-hexane IV. Saccharic acid
sol: NaHCO_{3}: glucose is not an acid → no reaction. HNO_{3} oxidises both ends → saccharic (glucaric) acid.
HI/heat reduces fully → n-hexane (straight chain proof). Br_{2} water (mild) oxidises only –CHO → gluconic acid.

pyq.q: Match List - I (Reaction of Glucose with) with List - II (Product formed): A. Hydroxylamine B. Br_{2} water C. Excess acetic anhydride D. Concentrated HNO_{3}; I. Gluconic acid II. Glucose pentacetate III. Saccharic acid IV. Glucoxime
sol: NH_{2}OH condenses with –CHO → oxime. Br_{2} water → gluconic acid.
Ac_{2}O acetylates all five –OH → pentaacetate. HNO_{3} → saccharic acid.

pyq.q: Identify the correct statements. A. Glucose exists in two anomeric forms. B. Anomers of glucose differ in configuration at C−1 in cyclic hemiacetal structure. C. Melting point of α-anomer of glucose is greater than β-anomer. D. Specific rotation of α-anomer is +19° while for β-anomer is +112°. E. α and β-anomers of glucose are prepared by crystallization of saturated glucose solution at 303 K and 371 K respectively.
sol: α and β glucose differ only at C1 (A, B true). Melting points: α 419 K, β 423 K → C false.
Rotations: α +112°, β +19° (D swapped, false). Crystallising at 303 K gives α, at 371 K gives β (E true).

pyq.q: The incorrect statement from the following with respect to carbohydrates is :
sol: Oligosaccharides can contain different units: sucrose → glucose + fructose, lactose → glucose + galactose. So "always the same" is wrong.
All monosaccharides (aldoses and ketoses) reduce Tollens/Fehling.
o: The monosaccharide units obtained from hydrolysis of oligosaccharides are always the same.
Starch and cellulose are typical examples of polysaccharides, which are very high molecular weight compounds of more than ten monosaccharide units.
Open chain and cyclic structures co-exist at equilibrium that are responsible for certain properties as in the case of D-(+)-glucose.

pyq.q: Both human DNA and RNA are chiral molecules. The chirality in DNA and RNA arises due to the presence of
sol: Bases are flat and achiral; phosphate is not a stereocentre.
The pentose (β-D-ribose / β-D-2-deoxyribose) carries the stereocentres → chirality.

pyq.q: The number of tripeptides formed by three different amino acids using each amino acid once is
sol: Each tripeptide is an ordered sequence (N-terminus → C-terminus).
Arrangements of 3 different residues: 3! = 6.

pyq.q: The number of possible tripeptides formed involving alanine (ala), glycine (gly) and valine (val), where no amino acid has been used more than once is:
sol: All three residues, each once: 3! orderings.
Ala-Gly-Val, Ala-Val-Gly, Gly-Ala-Val, Gly-Val-Ala, Val-Ala-Gly, Val-Gly-Ala → 6.

pyq.q: A tetrapeptide, "x" on complete hydrolysis produced glycine (Gly), alanine (Ala), valine (Val), leucine (Leu) in equimolar proportion each. The number of tetrapeptides (sequences) possible involving each of these amino acids is :
sol: Four different residues, each once, in order: 4! = 24.

pyq.q: Identify the correct statement among the following :
sol: (1) glycine is achiral. (2) threonine and isoleucine have TWO chiral centres. (4) aspartic acid also has a side-chain –COOH.
(3) two –SH groups oxidise to a –S–S– bridge → cystine. Correct.
o: All naturally occurring amino acids are optically active.
All naturally occurring amino acids except glycine contain one chiral centre.
Amino acid, cysteine can easily undergo dimerisation due to the presence of free SH group.
Glutamic acid is the only amino acid that contains a −COOH group at the side chain.

pyq.q: Identify the pair of reactants that upon reaction, with elimination of HCl will give rise to the dipeptide Gly-Ala.
sol: A peptide is written N-terminus first: Gly-Ala means glycine supplies the C=O, alanine supplies the N–H.
So the acid chloride must be glycyl chloride (H_{2}NCH_{2}COCl) and the amine part alanine → option 2.

pyq.q: A dipeptide, "x" on complete hydrolysis gives "y" and "z". "y" on treatment with aq. HNO_{2} produces lactic acid. On the other hand "z" on heating gives the following cyclic molecule: a six-membered 2,5-diketopiperazine with no side chains (–NH–CH_{2}–CO– units only). Based on the information given, the dipeptide x is:
sol: HNO_{2} turns H_{2}N–CHR–COOH into HO–CHR–COOH. Lactic acid is CH_{3}CH(OH)COOH → R = CH_{3} → y = alanine.
Two glycines condense to the unsubstituted diketopiperazine → z = glycine. x = Ala-Gly.

pyq.q: Coagulation of egg, on heating is because of :
sol: Heat breaks the H-bonds that hold the secondary/tertiary folds: the globular albumin unfolds and clumps — denaturation.
Peptide bonds (primary structure) survive.
o: The secondary structure of protein remains unchanged
Breaking of peptide linkages in the primary structure

pyq.q: Which structure of protein remains intact after coagulation of egg white on boiling?
sol: Boiling breaks H-bonds / weak forces only.
The covalent peptide chain (amino-acid sequence = primary structure) is left intact.

pyq.q: Which of the following gives a positive test with ninhydrin?
sol: Ninhydrin gives a violet (Ruhemann's purple) colour with free α-amino groups of amino acids/proteins.
Only egg albumin is a protein.

pyq.q: The incorrect statements regarding enzymes are : (A) Enzymes are biocatalysts. (B) Enzymes are non-specific and can catalyse different kinds of reactions. (C) Most Enzymes are globular proteins. (D) Enzyme - oxidase catalyses the hydrolysis of maltose into glucose.
sol: Enzymes are highly SPECIFIC (B wrong).
Maltose → glucose is done by MALTASE; oxidases catalyse oxidations (D wrong). A and C are correct.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement (I) : On hydrolysis, oligo peptides give rise to fewer number of α-amino acids while proteins give rise to a large number of β-amino acids. Statement (II) : Natural proteins are denatured by acids which convert the water soluble form of fibrous proteins to their water insoluble form. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
sol: Proteins also give α-amino acids, not β. I wrong.
Denaturation turns water-soluble GLOBULAR proteins into insoluble fibrous ones; fibrous proteins are already insoluble. II wrong.
o: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

pyq.q: The total number of carbon atoms present in tyrosine, an amino acid, is________
sol: Tyrosine = p-HO–C_{6}H_{4}–CH_{2}–CH(NH_{2})–COOH.
Ring 6 + CH_{2} 1 + CH 1 + COOH 1 = 9 C.

pyq.q: Thyroxine, the hormone, has the structure HO–C_{6}H_{2}I_{2}–O–C_{6}H_{2}I_{2}–CH_{2}–CH(NH_{2})–COOH. The percentage of iodine in thyroxine is ____%. (nearest integer) (Given molar mass in g mol^{−1} C:12, H:1, O:16, N:14, I:127)
Identify the correct pair having amino acid (A) and the hormone (B) that is iodinated derivative of the amino acid (A). (T and Y represent one letter code for amino acids)
sol: Thyroxine is made in the thyroid by iodinating TYROSINE (one-letter code Y; T is threonine).
Insulin is a polypeptide, not an iodinated amino acid.

pyq.q: Total number of essential amino acid among the given list of amino acids is ______: Arginine, Phenylalanine, Aspartic acid, Cysteine, Histidine, Valine, Proline
sol: Essential (NCERT): valine, leucine, isoleucine, phenylalanine, tryptophan, threonine, methionine, lysine, arginine, histidine.
From the list: arginine, phenylalanine, histidine, valine → 4.

pyq.q: Identify the essential amino acids from below : (A) Valine (B) Proline (C) Lysine (D) Threonine (E) Tyrosine
sol: Valine, lysine, threonine must come from food.
Proline is made in the body; tyrosine is made from phenylalanine.

pyq.q: Identify the correct statements. A. Arginine and Tryptophan are essential amino acids. B. Histidine does not contain heterocyclic ring in its structure. C. Proline is a six membered cyclic ring amino acid. D. Glycine does not have chiral centre. E. Cysteine has characteristic feature of side chain as MeS–CH_{2}–CH_{2}–.
sol: A true. B false: histidine carries an imidazole ring. C false: proline's ring (pyrrolidine) is FIVE-membered.
D true (R = H). E false: CH_{3}S–CH_{2}CH_{2}– is methionine; cysteine has HS–CH_{2}–.

pyq.q: Match the LIST-I (Name of amino acid) with LIST-II (One letter symbol/type): A. Arginine B. Aspartic acid C. Lysine D. Glutamic acid; I. D/Non-essential II. R/Essential III. E/Non-essential IV. K/Essential
sol: One-letter codes: Arg R, Asp D, Lys K, Glu E.
Arg and Lys are essential; Asp and Glu are non-essential → A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

pyq.q: The α-Helix and β-Pleated sheet structures of protein are associated with its :
sol: Secondary structure = local shape held by C=O···H–N hydrogen bonds: α-helix and β-pleated sheet.

pyq.q: Identify the incorrect statement about tertiary structure of proteins.
sol: pH change alters charges on side chains, breaking salt bridges and H-bonds → the tertiary fold is lost (denaturation).
So "remains intact" is wrong; the other three describe tertiary structure correctly.
o: They can be fibrous or globular in structure.
The main forces that stabilize the structure are hydrogen bonding, disulphide links, van der Waals and electrostatic forces of attraction.
The structure remains intact when exposed to pH changes.
A linear polypeptide chain will convert to a secondary structure and then further folding of the secondary structure will convert to tertiary structure.

pyq.q: Type of amino acids obtained by hydrolysis of proteins is :
sol: In proteins –NH_{2} and –COOH sit on the same (α) carbon: hydrolysis gives α-amino acids.

pyq.q: Number of compounds among the following which contain sulphur as heteroatom is: Furan, Thiophene, Pyridine, Pyrrole, Cysteine, Tyrosine
sol: Furan has O, pyridine and pyrrole have N, tyrosine has no S.
Sulphur: thiophene (C_{4}H_{4}S) and cysteine (–CH_{2}SH) → 2.

pyq.q: Which of the following amino acid will give violet coloured complex with neutral ferric chloride solution?
sol: Neutral FeCl_{3} gives violet with a PHENOL (Ar–OH).
Only tyrosine has a phenolic –OH; threonine/serine have alcoholic –OH.

pyq.q: If one strand of a DNA has the sequence ATGCTTCA, sequence of the bases in complementary strand is:
sol: Pairing rules: A–T, G–C.
ATGCTTCA → TACGAAGT.

pyq.q: The total number of hydrogen bonds of a DNA double helix whose one strand has the following sequence of bases is ___________: 5'-G G C A A A T C G G C T A-3'
sol: G≡C pairs have 3 H-bonds, A=T pairs have 2.
G/C count = 7 → 21; A/T count = 6 → 12. Total 33.

pyq.q: Two nucleotides are joined together by a linkage known as :
sol: The phosphate links C5′ of one sugar to C3′ of the next: a phosphodiester bond.
The glycosidic bond joins base to sugar inside ONE nucleotide.

pyq.q: The total number of correct statements, regarding the nucleic acids is _______. A. RNA is regarded as the reserve of genetic information. B. DNA molecule self-duplicates during cell division. C. DNA synthesizes proteins in the cell. D. The message for the synthesis of particular proteins is present in DNA. E. Identical DNA strands are transferred to daughter cells.
sol: DNA (not RNA) is the reserve of genetic information (A false); RNA, not DNA, carries out protein synthesis (C false).
B, D, E are correct → 3.

pyq.q: Fat soluble vitamins are: A. Vitamin B_{1} B. Vitamin C C. Vitamin E D. Vitamin B_{12} E. Vitamin K
sol: Fat soluble: A, D, E, K. B-group and C are water soluble.
From the list: vitamin E (C) and vitamin K (E).

pyq.q: Match List - I (Vitamin) with List - II (Name): A. Vitamin B_{1} B. Vitamin B_{2} C. Vitamin B_{6} D. Vitamin C; I. Pyridoxine II. Ascorbic acid III. Thiamine IV. Riboflavin
sol: B_{1} thiamine, B_{2} riboflavin, B_{6} pyridoxine, C ascorbic acid.

pyq.q: Which of the following acids is a vitamin?
sol: Ascorbic acid is vitamin C. Adipic acid → nylon-6,6; aspartic acid is an amino acid; saccharic acid comes from oxidising glucose.

pyq.q: From the vitamins A, B_{1}, B_{6}, B_{12}, C, D, E and K, the number of vitamins that can be stored in our body is _____.
sol: Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) are stored in liver and adipose tissue.
Of the water-soluble ones only B_{12} is stored (in the liver). Total 5.

Alpha and beta forms differing at C1
